Suspected Acute Stroke — Guided Pathway

About this pathway

The Epic Suspected Acute Stroke SE pathway, rebuilt so you answer one question at a time and only see the branches your patient is actually on. Enter last known well and the screens; it works out Code Stroke vs non-emergent, the imaging order, and the thrombolytic and thrombectomy assessments, and produces a summary for the note.

Prototype for discussion
Clinical content is transcribed from the current Epic pathway. Purple items are Epic-native links that would need wiring if adopted; blue items are reference content that can live in the app; green items are documented in the app (NIHSS, mRS). Not a validated clinical decision tool.

Code Stroke Activation Criteria

LKW ≤ 4.5 Hours

Activate code stroke if NOT suspected peripheral etiology and any of:

  • SUDDEN trouble walking, loss of balance or coordination
  • SUDDEN trouble seeing in one or both eyes
  • SUDDEN numbness or weakness on one side of the body
  • SUDDEN confusion, trouble speaking or understanding
  • SUDDEN severe headache with no known cause + neuro symptoms
  • SUDDEN, unexplained comatose-like state

LKW >4.5 – 24 Hours

  • Sudden, unexplained comatose-like state, OR
  • FANG-D positive (see FANG-D tab), OR
  • Disabling symptoms — deficits that would prevent return to baseline work or ADLs

LKW >24 Hours or Resolved Symptoms

No code stroke. Non-emergent imaging only. No CT perfusion role.

FANG-D Score: Qualitative LVO Screen

FANG-D positive = any ONE of the following:
Used for code stroke activation (>4.5h) and imaging determination
LetterDeficitDetails
FField cutComplete hemianopsia
AAphasiaSevere aphasia (can't communicate meaningfully)
NNeglectSevere hemi-attention / extinction to >1 modality
GGaze preferenceForced eye deviation or gaze preference
DDense weaknessAny weakness limiting sustained effort against gravity
Clinical Pearl
NIHSS ≥6 generally captures disabling deficits, but specific deficits (isolated hemianopsia, severe aphasia) may be disabling even at NIHSS <6.

NOT Clearly Disabling (IVT may not benefit)

  • Isolated facial droop
  • Hemisensory loss only
  • Mild cortical hand weakness (esp. nondominant)
  • Mild hemimotor or hemisensorimotor loss
  • Mild hemiataxia (still ambulatory)
  • Isolated mild aphasia (still communicates meaningfully)

Can the patient do ADLs (Bathing, Ambulating, Toileting, Hygiene, Eating) if deficits persist?

Imaging Protocol by Time Window & FANG-D

Time from LKWFANG-D StatusImaging Order
<4.5 hoursFANG-D NegativeCT Code Stroke Head W/O only. In select cases, may add CTA H&N
<4.5 hoursFANG-D PositiveCT Code Stroke WITH Perfusion (NCCT + CTA H&N + CTP)
4.5–24 hoursFANG-D PositiveCT Code Stroke WITH Perfusion (NCCT + CTA H&N + CTP)
4.5–24 hoursFANG-D NegativeNon-emergent (CT head W/O ± CTA H&N). No CTP.
>24 hoursAnyNon-emergent brain imaging. No CTP role.
Tip
If ordering CTA chest dissection protocol, also recommend CTA head and neck.

Perfusion Triggers — Reconciled with the Code Stroke Pathway

The table above keys imaging off FANG-D alone. The Suspected Acute Stroke pathway triggers perfusion imaging on a wider set, because each identifies a possible thrombectomy candidate:

  • LVO screen (FANG-D) positive — field cut, aphasia, neglect, gaze preference, dense limb weakness
  • BAO screen positive — sudden, unexplained comatose-like state
  • Disabling symptoms — deficits that would prevent return to baseline work or ADLs

Any one of these puts the patient in the CT Code Stroke WITH Perfusion row (NCCT + CTA H&N + CTP) for both the <4.5 hour and 4.5–24 hour windows — if CTP is available at your site.

LKW Unknown
Treated as the 4.5–24 hour row. An unknown-LKW patient with any perfusion trigger still gets CTP; with none, imaging is non-emergent.
Let the pathway work this out
The Guided Pathway tab computes the imaging order from the LKW and screens you enter, states which row it matched, and says which trigger fired — no cross-referencing mid-code.

IV TNK Within 4.5 Hours (AHA 2026 Class I)

Eligibility

  • Age ≥ 18 years
  • Measurable, disabling neurologic deficit
  • Symptom onset (or LKW) ≤ 4.5 hours
  • No hemorrhage on NCCT
  • No contraindications (see TNK Contraindications tab)
AHA 2026 Key Update
Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg is recommended (Class I). Initiate ASAP. Do NOT delay for CTA/CTP or MRI within 4.5h — NCCT alone is sufficient.

Examples of Clearly Disabling Deficits (IVT Indicated)

  • NIHSS ≥ 6
  • Complete hemianopsia
  • Severe aphasia (inability to communicate meaningfully)
  • Severe hemi-attention or extinction to >1 modality (neglect)
  • Forced eye deviation or gaze preference
  • Any weakness limiting sustained effort against gravity

Examples of NOT Clearly Disabling Deficits (IVT May NOT Benefit)

Class 3: No Benefit for IVT
For non-disabling deficits, trials failed to show IVT benefit. Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is preferred.
  • Isolated facial droop
  • Hemisensory loss only
  • Mild cortical hand weakness (esp. nondominant, NIHSS 0 in motor)
  • Mild hemimotor or hemisensorimotor loss
  • Mild hemiataxia (still ambulatory)
  • Isolated mild aphasia (still communicates meaningfully)

Can the patient do ADLs (Bathing, Ambulating, Toileting, Hygiene, Eating) if deficits persist?

Conditions Where Benefits of IVT > Risks of Bleeding

These conditions should NOT prevent IVT if the patient otherwise meets eligibility:

ConditionConsideration
Extracranial cervical dissectionsReasonably safe within 4.5 h and probably recommended
Extra-axial intracranial neoplasmsRisk of harm is likely low; benefit likely outweighs risk
Angiographic procedural strokeIVT during or immediately post-angiography should be considered
Unruptured intracranial aneurysmRisk of harm is likely low; benefit likely outweighs risk
History of GI/GU bleedingPrevious remote history that is stable — consider on individual basis with GI/GU consultation
History of MIIVT probably has greater benefit than risk
Recreational drug useIVT probably has greater benefit than risk in most patients
Uncertainty of stroke diagnosis / mimicsUnless absolute contraindications exist, risk of harm is low; benefit likely outweighs risk
Moya-Moya diseaseDoes not appear to increase ICH risk; benefit likely outweighs risk

TNK Contraindications (AHA 2026)

Absolute Contraindications

ConditionDetails
CT with extensive hypodensityBrain imaging shows clear hypodensity responsible for symptoms (density greater than contralateral unaffected white matter)
CT with hemorrhageCT reveals acute intracranial hemorrhage
Moderate–severe TBI <14 daysTBI within 14 days with >30 min unconsciousness, GCS <13, or evidence of hemorrhage/contusion/skull fracture
Neurosurgery <14 daysIntracranial/spinal surgery within 14 days — IVT potentially harmful
Acute spinal cord injury within 3 monthsIVT is likely contraindicated
Intra-axial neoplasmPatients harboring intra-axial intracranial neoplasm — IVT potentially harmful
Infective endocarditisActive infective endocarditis — IVT should not be administered
Severe coagulopathy / thrombocytopeniaPLT <100K, INR >1.7, aPTT >40s, or PT >15s. Can initiate IVT before labs if no recent anticoagulant use, but stop if results abnormal.
Aortic arch dissectionKnown or suspected — IVT is potentially harmful
Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA)Patients on amyloid immunotherapy or with ARIA — ICH risk unknown, IVT should be avoided

Relative Contraindications (Individualized Risk–Benefit)

Require careful individualized assessment. IVT may be considered after weighing stroke severity vs bleeding risk:

ConditionConsideration
Pre-existing disabilityBenefits vs risks uncertain with pre-existing disability/frailty. Determine on individual basis.
DOAC exposure (<48 h)Safety unknown. Consider timing, renal function, severity, reversal agents, anti-factor Xa/thrombin assays.
Ischemic stroke within 3 monthsMay increase ICH risk. Weigh timing/size of prior stroke vs benefits. Individualize.
Prior ICHMay increase sICH risk. CAA patients higher risk. ICH due to modifiable conditions may have greater benefit.
Recent major non-CNS trauma (14d–3mo)Increased risk of serious systemic hemorrhage. Individual consideration with surgical consultation.
Recent major non-CNS surgery w/in 10 daysIncreased risk. Individual consideration, surgical area, and surgical expert consultation.
Recent GI/GU bleeding w/in 21 daysIncreased risk. GI/GU consultation to determine if bleeding treated and risk reduced.
Intracranial arterial dissectionSafety of IVT is unknown
Intracranial vascular malformationsSafety with unruptured/untreated vascular malformation is unknown
Recent STEMI w/in 3 monthsIndividual risk/benefit with emergent cardiology consultation. Very recent STEMI: consider hemopericardium risk.
Acute pericarditisMay be reasonable for major AIS likely to produce severe disability. Emergent cardiology consultation.
Left atrial or ventricular thrombusMay be reasonable for major AIS likely to produce severe disability. Emergent cardiology consultation.
Systemic active malignancySafety unknown. Oncology consultation. Consider type, stage, and active complications.
Pregnancy and post-partum periodMay be considered when benefits outweigh uterine bleeding risk. Emergent obstetrical consultation.
Dural puncture w/in 7 daysMay be considered on individual basis
Arterial puncture noncompressible site w/in 7 daysSafety after puncture of noncompressible vessel (e.g., subclavian artery) is unknown
Moderate–severe TBI (≥14 days to 3 months)May be considered. Based on type/severity of injury with neurosurgical/neurocritical care input.
Neurosurgery ≥14 days to 3 monthsConsider on individual basis. Neurosurgical consultation recommended.
Key Principle
When in doubt — weigh severity and disability of the presenting stroke against bleeding risk. For severe, clearly disabling deficits, IVT benefit generally outweighs risk. Consultation with stroke neurology is recommended.

Guideline Note
The above serves as a local institutional guideline. Decision making for acute stroke treatment is complex and is best made by the treating team on an individual patient basis.

Extended Window IV TNK: Non-LVO / MeVO / DVO

4.5–24 hours • Based on OPTION trial • Limited to FANG-D positive patients

OPTION Trial (JAMA 2026)
IV TNK 0.25 mg/kg in non-LVO with salvageable tissue: mRS 0–1 at 90d: 43.6% vs 34.2% (RR 1.28, P=0.02, NNT=11). sICH: 2.8% vs 0%.

Inclusion Criteria

  • Age ≥ 18
  • FANG-D positive (local requirement)
  • NIHSS 6–25 (or 4–5 with disabling deficit)
  • Pre-stroke mRS 0 or 1
  • LKW 4.5 to 24 hours
  • Qualifying vessel: M2, M3-M4, ACA, PCA, stenosis, or vertebrobasilar occlusion not eligible for EVT
  • CTP mismatch: core <50 mL, ratio ≥1.2, mismatch vol ≥10 mL

Exclusion Criteria

  • Extensive hypodensity on NCCT (clear hypodensity responsible for symptoms — density greater than contralateral unaffected white matter)
  • NCCT hypodensity larger than CTP-defined ischemic core (mismatch inconsistency — significantly higher sICH risk)
  • LVO present (ICA, M1, or vertebrobasilar) AND planned EVT
  • Pre-stroke mRS > 1
  • No CTP mismatch
  • FANG-D negative (current local restriction)
Important
All absolute and relative contraindications for IV TNK within the standard 4.5-hour window (see TNK Contraindications tab) also apply to extended-window treatment. Review before administering.
Safety Note
sICH: 2.8% vs 0%. Two of 21 patients with NCCT hypodensity larger than perfusion-defined core developed sICH. Carefully evaluate NCCT alongside perfusion.
If CTP Not Available or Technically Limited
STAT MRI brain with DWI-FLAIR mismatch can be considered to determine eligibility: presence of DWI lesion with absence of corresponding FLAIR lesion indicates salvageable tissue.

Extended Window IV TNK: LVO (4.5–24h)

For patients NOT eligible for EVT or anticipated delay ≥60–90 min

Evidence
TRACE-III: TNK in LVO w/o EVT → mRS 0–1: 33% vs 24.2% (RR 1.37, P=0.03)
HOPE: Alteplase, no EVT → mRS 0–1: 40.3% vs 26.3% (aRR 1.52, P=0.004)
AHA 2026: Class 2b

When to Consider

  • NOT a candidate for EVT
  • Anticipated delay to groin puncture ≥ 60–90 min
  • At spoke/PSC without thrombectomy + prolonged transfer

Inclusion Criteria

  • Age ≥ 18
  • LVO: ICA, M1, M2 (TRACE-III); any occlusion (HOPE)
  • NIHSS 6–25 (TRACE-III) or 4–26 (HOPE)
  • Pre-stroke mRS 0 or 1
  • LKW 4.5 to 24 hours
  • CTP mismatch: core <70 mL, ratio ≥1.8 (TRACE-III) or ≥1.2 (HOPE), mismatch vol ≥15 or ≥10 mL
  • EVT NOT planned or delay ≥60–90 min

Do NOT Give Extended-Window IVT If:

  • EVT immediately available (within ~60 min)
  • Core ≥ 70 mL
  • No perfusion mismatch
  • Pre-stroke mRS ≥ 2
  • Standard IVT contraindications
  • Large NCCT hypodensity exceeding CTP core
Priority
If eligible for BOTH extended-window IVT AND EVT, EVT takes priority. IVT is bridging/standalone only when EVT unavailable or significantly delayed.

Which number do I use?
The banded chart above is for estimated weight — each row rounds up to the top of its band. If an actual weight is known, use the calculator (exact 0.25 mg/kg). A 61 kg patient is 15.3 mg by calculator, 17.5 mg by chart.
  • IV push over 5–10 seconds

Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) Quick Reference

The mRS measures the degree of disability or dependence in daily activities. Scores 0–2 are generally considered a "good outcome" in stroke trials. Pre-stroke mRS is critical for EVT eligibility decisions.

ScoreGradeDescriptionKey Functional Test
0 No symptoms No symptoms at all. Completely asymptomatic. Normal function
1 No significant disability Symptoms but able to carry out all usual duties and activities. All pre-stroke activities
2 Slight disability Unable to carry out all previous activities but able to look after own affairs without assistance. Independent in ADLs; cannot do all prior activities
3 Moderate disability Requires some help, but able to walk without assistance. Walks independently; needs help with some tasks
4 Moderately severe disability Unable to walk without assistance and unable to attend to own bodily needs without assistance. Cannot walk unassisted; cannot manage own bodily care
5 Severe disability Bedridden, incontinent and requiring constant nursing care and attention. Bedridden; requires 24h nursing care
6 Dead Death. —

mRS in Clinical Decision-Making

EVT Eligibility (Pre-stroke)

mRS 0–2 → Standard eligibility for most EVT windows
mRS 3–4 → Individualized basis if radiographic criteria met
mRS 5 → Generally not candidate

Outcome Benchmarks (Trial Endpoints)

mRS 0–1 → Excellent outcome (most IVT trials)
mRS 0–2 → Functional independence (EVT trials)
mRS 0–3 → Ambulatory (large-core EVT trials)

IVT Extended Window (Pre-stroke)

mRS 0–1 → Required for TRACE-III, HOPE extended-window IVT
mRS 0–1 → Required for OPTION (non-LVO, 4.5–24h)

Practical Tip
When pre-stroke mRS is unknown, ask family/EMS: "Before this stroke, could the patient walk, dress, and manage their own affairs independently?" — Yes → likely mRS 0–2. Confirm with collateral history before proceeding with treatment.

Post-Thrombolysis Monitoring

  • Admit to ICU or stroke unit
  • BP + neuro checks: q15 min × 2h → q30 min × 6h → q1h until 24h
  • Keep SBP <180, DBP <105 post-IVT
  • Do NOT target SBP <140 (Class 3: No Benefit)
  • Delay NG tubes, Foley, arterial lines if safely manageable
  • If severe HA, acute HTN, N/V, or worsening exam → STOP infusion → STAT CT head
  • Follow-up CT/MRI at 24 hours before starting antiplatelets/anticoagulants

Summary
Multiple RCTs confirmed TNK 0.25 mg/kg is non-inferior to alteplase within 4.5 h. TNK's single IV bolus (5–10 sec) vs alteplase's 1-hour infusion simplifies administration, reduces dosing errors, and shortens DTN/DIDO times — supporting AHA 2026 Class I for either agent.

Meta-Analysis (Liu et al., Neurology 2025)
Across 6 large-core RCTs (n=1,887): EVT improved ordinal mRS (gOR 1.6, 95% CI 1.4–1.8), independent ambulation (mRS 0–3: RR 1.9), and reduced mortality (RR 0.9) despite higher sICH (RR 1.7). Benefit decreased with longer onset-to-treatment time.

STAT Neurologic Consult Criteria
Conditions requiring urgent neurology consultation regardless of stroke pathway
  1. Large hemispheric stroke with possibility of swelling
    • Higher concern in patients < 60 years
  2. Stroke symptoms with onset outside of 24-hour window AND acute decline in mental status
  3. Multiple seizures and/or possible Status epilepticus without improvement of mental status within 30 minutes
    • Not following commands
    • No withdrawal to painful stimulus
  4. Acute, unexplained change in mental status without return to baseline
  5. Potential acute non-traumatic spinal cord pathology
  6. Neuromuscular emergencies and/or neurological disorders causing impaired breathing
  7. Newly diagnosed intracranial venous/sinus thrombosis
